title: Sextus Pompeius Festus, De verborum significatu (surviving Codex Farnesianus, M–V) — On the Meaning of Words; Фест, «О значении слов». Proposed unit: letter M
author: Sextus Pompeius Festus (epitomising Verrius Flaccus)
size: c. 3,300 entries overall; Lindsay 1913 c. 520 pp. incl. Paulus; Festus' own text est. 50–60k words (estimate)
edition: Lindsay, Teubner 1913; Thewrewk 1889 (both public domain; Thewrewk scan on sourcelibrary.org)
ru_evidence: Only Paul the Deacon's epitome: A. A. Pavlov (Сыктывкар 2012, 300 pp.; selections in ВДИ 2012 №2), per ru.wikipedia. No Russian translation of Festus' own text found
en_evidence: None published. The UCL Festus Lexicon Project and B. Fortson's ACLS 2026 fellowship are working on the 'first-ever full English translation'
value: Unique store of Verrius Flaccus' material: archaic Latin, Roman religion and ritual, law, topography and early Roman history. Constantly cited by historians of religion and law and by linguists
ai_feasibility: medium — lacunose manuscript with modern supplements and archaic quotations; restorations must be marked conservatively
pilot_unit: Letter M (Festus with parallel Paulus entries), est. 8–10k words
